options.text: Aribam Syam Sharma - Jakhan Choto Chilam

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**JB Kripalani- My Times**__

__
 
• Acharya Kripalani was born in Hyderabad in Sind in 1888.
 
• He studied in Bombay and Pune and briefly taught at Muzaffarpur College in Bihar and Banaras Hindu University.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Kripalani sheds light on the relationship he shared with legendary figures such as Jawaharlal Nehru, Subhas Chandra Bose, Maulana Azad, Sardar Patel, and of course, Mahatma Gandhi.

questions.question: Surendranath Banerjee's autobiography is called ____________
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __A Nation in the Making__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sir Surendranath Banerjee **often known as **Rashtraguru **was an **Indian nationalist leader **during **British Rule**.
 
• He **founded **a **nationalist organization **called the **Indian National Association **and was **one of the founding members **of the **Indian National Congress**.
 
• **Surendranath supported Montagu**–Chelmsford Reforms, unlike Congress, and with many liberal leaders he left Congress and founded a new organization **named Indian National Liberation Federation in 1919**.
 
• **Surendranath Banerjee **was **born **in **Calcutta**, in the province of **Bengal **to a **Rarhi Kulin Brahmin family**, suggesting that the ancestral seat of the family was in the **Rarh region **of present-day **West Bengal**.
 
• **In 1879**, he bought the **newspaper**, **The Bengalee**(founded in 1862 by Girish Chandra Ghosh) and edited it for 40 years in b, when Banerjee was arrested for publishing remarks in his paper.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **A Nation in the Making **written in the **last years of Sir Surendranath Banerjea's life**, is not only the autobiography of a **pioneering leader **in **Indian politics **but also a **commentary on public life**.
 
• **This book **is originally **published **in **1925**.

questions.question: ‘Jakhan Choto Chilam’ is an autobiography written in the Bengali language by which of the following Indian Bangla film directors?

__
 
• ‘**Jakhan Choto Chilam**’ is an autobiography written in the Bengali language by **Satyajit Ray**.
 
• In this book, Satyajit Ray discusses his childhood days in the city of **Kolkata** (then Calcutta), India from the eyes of an everyday boy.
 
• **Satyajit Ray **was an Indian director, screenwriter, documentary filmmaker, author, essayist, lyricist, magazine editor, illustrator, calligrapher, and music composer.
 
• **Satyajit Ray** received many major awards in his career, including 36 Indian National Film Awards, a Golden Lion, a Golden Bear, 2 Silver Bears, many additional awards at international film festivals and ceremonies, and an Academy Honorary Award in **1992**.
 
• In 1978, he was awarded an honorary degree by **Oxford University**.
 
• In 1992, Government of India honored him the **Bharat Ratna** Award.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rituparno Ghosh** was an Indian film director, actor, writer, and lyricist. After pursuing a degree in economics, he started his career as a creative artist at an advertising agency.
 
• **Mrinal Sen** was an Indian film director of Bengali heritage and a nominated Member of the Indian parliament. 
 
• **Tapan Sinha **was one of the most prominent Indian film directors of his time forming a legendary quartet with Satyajit Ray, Ritwik Ghatak, and Mrinal Sen.

questions.question: Which Indian writer wrote the famous book "Mansarovar"?
questions.solution:
the correct answer is __**Premchand**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Premchand

 
 
• Premchand, also known as Dhanpat Rai Srivastava, was an Indian author best known for his contemporary Hindustani writing.
 
• He was born on July 31, 1880, and died on October 8, 1936.
 
• Hindi and Urdu social fiction were invented by Premchand.
 
• He was one of the first writers to discuss caste systems, the suffering of working women, and other issues that were prevalent in late 1880s culture.
 
• He is one of the most well-known authors on the Indian continent and is recognised as one of the greatest Hindi authors of the first half of the 20th century. 
 
• He has written various novels, including, Godaan, Karmabhoomi, Gaban, Mansarovar, and Idgah.
 
• In a book titled Soz-e-Watan, he released his first collection of five short stories.
